claim_boundary.approved_claim: One pinned WebGoat IDOR benchmark scenario has raw-free, source-bound CWE-639 and authorization-bypass mechanism evidence from two verified Git blobs; CVSS, registry admission, scanner accuracy, L2 completion, and release remain unproven.

decision_contract.blocked: Use only when the assigned provider or review path is unavailable.
decision_contract.go: Use only when the supplied evidence and assigned scope reveal no material source-binding, anchor-validation, CWE-mapping, raw-free, repeatability, or claim-boundary defect.
decision_contract.hold: Use when a material defect or a false severity/release claim remains.

implementation_contract.anchors: The adapter reads the two exact pinned Git blobs, checks their content digest and required anchor IDs, and emits identifiers only rather than raw source text.
implementation_contract.classification: CWE-639 mapping is benchmark-scenario scoped; cvss_v4 and expected disposition stay null until separately source-bound asset-impact evidence exists.
implementation_contract.source: The immutable source receipt and pinned repository commit/tree must agree before blob extraction.

review_questions: Does the adapter bind both required Git blobs to the pinned source receipt and reject missing or altered anchors before emitting evidence?
Does the CWE-639 mapping fit the source-bound user-controlled cross-user profile access evidence without exposing raw source?
Does the explicit CVSS/release nonclaim prevent source classification from becoming an unjustified customer-deployment severity or release decision?
Do repeatability and test evidence support only this narrow subfield?

full_regression.first_run_failure: one SCA timeout test failure retained as residual instability
